standardsFrameworkItems.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

standardsFrameworkItemsbuildsTowards.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach. *For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?*

Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

buildsTowardsStandardsFrameworkItems.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context. *For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.*
Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).
Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. *For example, find the points of intersection between the line $y = -3x$ and the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 3$.*

Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Socioeconomic Status (SES) refers to a combination of factors, including a family's education and income compared to other families.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Mathematical Flexibility
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Mathematical Flexibility is the ability to maintain and shift among multiple representations of numbers and between problem-solving strategies in an adaptive manner.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Math Communication
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Language and literacy skills support many aspects of math problem solving.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Geometric Reasoning
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Geometric Reasoning involves using abstract thinking to define, analyze, and make arguments about shapes and spatial relationships.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Proportional Reasoning
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Proportional Reasoning involves an understanding of ratio and the relationships between ratios.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Statistical Reasoning
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Statistical Reasoning involves thinking about and understanding uncertainty and building mental models to capture key aspects of real world phenomena.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Social Awareness & Relationship Skills
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Learning is powerful when it is social––when we learn with and from each other.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Emotion
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Emotions are complex psychological states stemming from our positive and negative experiences.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Sense of Belonging
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: A Sense of Belonging allows us to feel included, respected, and supported in school.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Motivation
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Motivation is the desire and energy that guides behavior.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Working Memory
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: While the executive functions Inhibition and Working Memory are very much related processes and show similar developmental trajectories in childhood, they become more distinct processes during adolescence.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Reasoning
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Reasoning is the ability to think abstractly, draw inferences, identify patterns and relationships, and apply logic in order to flexibly solve novel problems.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Spatial Skills
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: We use our Spatial Skills to mentally manipulate objects and numbers.

factorsrelevantToStandard.name: Operations
factorsrelevantToStandard.description: Students typically begin by thinking about Operations as telling them which computations to do (such as finding the sum or difference of two numbers).

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Collaborative Problem Solving
strategiestargetsFactor.description: As students solve problems in a group, they learn new strategies and practice communicating their mathematical thinking.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Cognitively Demanding Tasks
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Providing math tasks with high cognitive demand conveys high expectations for all students by challenging them to engage in higher-order thinking.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Cumulative Review
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Continual use of foundational skills with different problems reinforces a conceptual understanding of math skills.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Creating Visual Representations
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Students activate more cognitive processes by exploring and representing their understandings in visual form.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Direct Instruction: Patterning
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Thinking of and about patterns encourages learners to look for and understand the rules and relationships that are critical components of mathematical reasoning.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Direct Instruction: Problem-solving Strategies
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Discussing strategies for solving mathematics problems after initially letting students attempt to problem solve on their own helps them understand how to organize their Algebraic Thinking and intentionally tackle problems.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Concrete-Representational-Abstract (CRA)
strategiestargetsFactor.description: CRA is a sequential instructional approach during which students move from working with concrete materials to creating representational drawings to using abstract symbols.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Error Analysis
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Analyzing incorrect worked examples is especially beneficial for helping students develop a conceptual understanding of mathematical processes.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Explaining Their Thinking
strategiestargetsFactor.description: When students explain their thinking process aloud with guidance in response to questions or prompts, they recognize the strategies they use and solidify their understanding.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Flexible Grouping
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Flexible grouping is a classroom practice that temporarily places students together in given groups to work together, with the purpose of achieving a given learning goal or activity.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Daily Review
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Daily review strengthens previous learning and can lead to fluent recall.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Individual Deliberate Practice
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Practicing until achieving several error-free attempts is critical for retention.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Guided Inquiry
strategiestargetsFactor.description: In guided inquiry, teachers help students use their own language for constructing knowledge by active listening and questioning.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Math Centers
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Math centers with math games, manipulatives, and activities support learner interests and promote the development of more complex math skills and social interactions.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Model Assignment or Skill
strategiestargetsFactor.description: By talking through their thinking at each step of a process, teachers can model what learning looks like.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Math Talks
strategiestargetsFactor.description: When students have meaningful discussions about math and use math vocabulary, they develop the thinking, questioning, and explanation skills needed to master mathematical concepts.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Direct Instruction: Problem Structures
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Teaching students to recognize the structures of algebraic representations helps them transfer solution methods from familiar to unfamiliar problems.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Multiple Representations: Manipulatives
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Providing physical and virtual representations of numbers and math concepts helps activate mental processes.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Multiple Representations: Visual Representations
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Visual representations help students understand what a number represents as well as recognize relationships between numbers.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Multimodal Instruction
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Instruction in multiple formats allows students to activate different cognitive skills to understand and remember the steps they are to take in their math work.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Self-instructions
strategiestargetsFactor.description: When students engage in a dialogue with themselves, they are able to orient, organize, and focus their thinking.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Self-monitoring
strategiestargetsFactor.description: When students monitor their comprehension, behavior, or use of strategies, they build their Metacognition.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Strengths-based Approach
strategiestargetsFactor.description: A strengths-based approach is one where educators intentionally identify, communicate, and harness students' assets, across many aspects of the whole child, in order to empower them to flourish.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Think-Pair-Share
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Students deepen their math understanding as they use and hear others use specific math language in informal ways.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Untimed Tests
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Untimed tests provide students the opportunity to flexibly and productively work with numbers, further developing their problem-solving abilities.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Worked Examples
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Analyzing and discussing solved problems helps students develop a deeper understanding of abstract mathematical processes.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Gestures
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Adding motions to complement learning activates more cognitive processes for recall and understanding.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Guided Practice
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Spending time with new content helps move concepts and ideas into Long-term Memory.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Jigsaw
strategiestargetsFactor.description: As students work with and process information by discussing, organizing, and sharing it together, they deepen their understanding.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Math Games
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Math games allow students to practice many math skills in a fun, applied context.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Math Songs
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Rhyming, alliteration, and other sound devices reinforce math skills development by activating the mental processes that promote memory.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Multiple Methods of Assessment
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Using multiple methods of assessment can help educators gain a comprehensive understanding of learner progress across a wide range of skills and content.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Peer Teaching
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Having students teach their knowledge, skills, and understanding to their classmates strengthens learning.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Pre-Assessment
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Pre-assessments are tools or activities used before instruction begins to help educators understand what students already know, understand, or can do—and where they may need support.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Project-based Learning
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Project-based learning (PBL) actively engages learners in authentic tasks designed to create products that answer a given question or solve a problem.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Real-world Math
strategiestargetsFactor.description: When teachers connect math to the students' world, students see how math is relevant and applicable to their daily lives.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Reciprocal Teaching
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Students deepen their understanding and gain confidence in their learning when they explain to and receive feedback from others.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Rich Resources: Audio & Braille
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Math games and manipulatives for vision differences support math development for learners with visual needs.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Rich Resources: Children's Literature
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Children's literature can be a welcoming way to help students learn math vocabulary and concepts.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Student-generated Problems
strategiestargetsFactor.description: When students create their own number and word problems, they connect math concepts to their background knowledge and lived experiences.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Translanguaging
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Translanguaging is a flexible classroom practice enabling students to listen, speak, read, and write across their multiple languages or dialects, even if the teacher does not have formal knowledge of these additional languages.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Videos
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Providing visuals to introduce, support, or review instruction activates more cognitive processes to support learning.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Writing to Learn Math
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Writing that encourages students to articulate their understanding of math concepts or explain math ideas helps deepen students' mathematical understanding.

interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Cognitive Flexibility, a component of executive functioning, is the ability to effectively adapt our behavior as we face changing environmental and task demands.

interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Long-term Memory can store information indefinitely.

standardsFrameworkItemsbuildsTowards.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

strategiestargetsFactor.description: Translanguaging is a flexible classroom practice enabling students to listen, speak, read, and write across their multiple languages or dialects, even if the teacher does not have formal knowledge of these additional languages.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Videos
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Providing visuals to introduce, support, or review instruction activates more cognitive processes to support learning.

strategiestargetsFactor.name: Writing to Learn Math
strategiestargetsFactor.description: Writing that encourages students to articulate their understanding of math concepts or explain math ideas helps deepen students' mathematical understanding.

learnerModelshasFactor.name: Building Math 7-10
learnerModelshasFactor.description: The goals for students’ math skills in Grades 7-10 include strengthening their abstract reasoning and constructing and communicating arguments using math. Understanding the Learner Factors and strategies that impact math skills and how they connect to each other can help you build tools and lessons that support all learners.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Physical Well-being
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: The benefits of physical health go beyond our bodies—our cognitive skills also improve with physical fitness.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Mathematical Flexibility
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Mathematical Flexibility is the ability to maintain and shift among multiple representations of numbers and between problem-solving strategies in an adaptive manner.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Math Communication
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Language and literacy skills support many aspects of math problem solving.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Proportional Reasoning
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Proportional Reasoning involves an understanding of ratio and the relationships between ratios.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Emotion
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Emotions are complex psychological states stemming from our positive and negative experiences.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Motivation
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Motivation is the desire and energy that guides behavior.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Math Mindset
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Math Mindset includes learners' self-concept and self-efficacy beliefs as well as their mindset toward failure, all of which shape their willingness to get involved with mathematics.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Stereotype Threat
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: In our society, there are many stereotypes that exist about the academic abilities of learners based on characteristics such as their race, gender, disability, and socioeconomic status.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Metacognition
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Metacognition refers to the ability to think about our own thinking and to pay attention to and control our cognitive processes.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Cognitive Flexibility
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Cognitive Flexibility, a component of executive functioning, is the ability to effectively adapt our behavior as we face changing environmental and task demands.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Long-term Memory
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Long-term Memory can store information indefinitely.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Reasoning
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Reasoning is the ability to think abstractly, draw inferences, identify patterns and relationships, and apply logic in order to flexibly solve novel problems.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Visual Processing
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: Visual Processing is seeing at the cognitive level: taking the input that comes through our Vision and working to understand what we see.

interactsWithFactorFactors.name: Spatial Skills
interactsWithFactorFactors.description: We use our Spatial Skills to mentally manipulate objects and numbers.
